Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:12:1.english: Does [the Mishnah] teach "There is no [difference] between" - [which would imply] that it is exhaustive and [the Tanna] did not omit anything?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:12:2.hebrew: קתני - קצת דברים שזו מרובה על זו, ושייר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:12:2.english: It teaches - some things in which this [double payment] is greater than that [fourfold and fivefold payment], and [the Tanna] omitted [others].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:15:1.english: As they are compared to land - For it is written: "And you shall bequeath them, etc." (Leviticus 25).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:15:2.english: They themselves are not money - Rather, they cause [one] to collect money.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:5:1.hebrew: למעלה מעשרים אמה - לא חזו לה אינשי ולא מפרסם ניסא, ואנן לפרסומי ניסא בעינן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:5:1.english: Higher than twenty cubits - People do not see it and the miracle is not publicized, whereas we require publicizing the miracle.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:8:1.hebrew: מרובה - אין הגונב אחר הגנב כו'. דכתיב "וגונב מבית האיש", ולא מבית הגנב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:8:1.english: Merubeh - One who steals after a thief, etc. For it is written, "and it is stolen from the house of the man," and not from the house of the thief.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:9:1.hebrew: בטוען טענת גנב - גנב בא וגנבו, ודרשינן לקמן בשמעתין דחייבו רחמנא כפילא אם נשבע ונמצא שקרן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:9:1.english: In [the case of] one who states the claim of a thief - [Claiming that] a thief came and stole it; and we expound later in our sugya that the Merciful One obligated him [to pay] double if he took an oath and was found [to be] a liar.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:9:2.hebrew: לא קתני - אלמא נהגי ד' וה' בטוען טענת גנב, אם טבח ומכר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 62b:9:2.english: It does not teach - Thus, [the payments of] fourfold and fivefold apply to one who claims [that] a thief [stole the deposit], if he slaughtered or sold [it].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:12:1.hebrew: מרובה קתני תנא ושייר - לשון ראשון דמייתי סייעתא, לא בעי למימר דשייר, דסבר ההוא לישנא דכיון דקתני "מרובה", אין לומר שייר, כמו ב"אין בין". וכן משמע הלשון דקאמר ללישנא בתרא: "מי קתני אין בין? מרובה קתני" — משמע שתחילה היה סבור ד"מרובה" הוי כמו "אין בין". וא"ת: ומאי שייר דהאי שייר? וי"ל: דשייר טענת גנב באבידה, דדריש לקמן רבי יוחנן דמשלם כפל, ואי טעין טענת גנב בפקדון לא משלם ארבעה וחמשה בטבח ומכר; הכי נמי טוען טענת גנב באבידה. ועוד, שמשייר שותף שגנב מחבירו, ושותפין שגנבו לא משלם ארבעה וחמשה, כדאמר לקמן בפירקין (בבא קמא ד' עח:). ועוד יש מפרשים דאין לחוש הכא אם אינו משייר כי אם דבר אחד, כיון דלא נחת למניינא, אלא דגלי לן שיש ריבוי בכפל מארבעה וחמשה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:12:1.english: "[The Mishnah] teaches 'more broadly,' [meaning] it taught [one case] and omitted [others]" - The first version, which brings a support [from the Mishnah], did not want to say that it omitted [anything], because that version held that since [the Mishnah] teaches "more broadly," one cannot say "it omitted," just as in [a Mishnah that teaches] "there is no difference between." And so too is implied by the wording that [the Gemara] states according to the latter version: "Does it teach 'there is no difference between'? It teaches 'more broadly'!" — this implies that initially it thought that "more broadly" is like "there is no difference between." And if you ask: What else did it omit, that it omitted this? One can answer: It omitted [the case of] a claim of theft regarding a lost object, for Rabbi Yochanan expounds below that [such a person] pays double, and [just as] if one makes a claim of theft regarding a deposit, he does not pay fourfold or fivefold when he slaughters or sells [it], so too [is the law for] one who makes a claim of theft regarding a lost object. And furthermore, it omitted [the case of] a partner who stole from his fellow, as partners who steal do not pay fourfold or fivefold, as [the Gemara] says later in our chapter (Bava Kamma 78b). And furthermore, there are those who explain that here we need not be concerned if it omits only one thing, since it did not set out to enumerate [a list], rather it merely reveals to us that there is a greater scope in double [payment] than in fourfold and fivefold [payment].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:15:1.hebrew: יצאו קרקעות כו' - וא"ת: כיון דאמעיטי משבועה כדאמרינן בפרק הזהב (ב"מ ד' נז:), תיפוק ליה דאין בהם כפל בטוען טענת גנב, דלא משלם אלא בשבועה כדאמרינן לקמן בשמעתין? וליכא למימר דאצטריך לקופץ ונשבע, דבהגוזל קמא (לקמן בבא קמא ד' קו.) מוכח דלא משלם אא"כ ב"ד משביעין אותו. וי"ל דאצטריך להיכא דנשבע ע"י גלגול, כדתנן (קדושין ד' כו.): "זוקקין הנכסים שיש להם אחריות עם הנכסים כו' לישבע עליהן". ומיהו לפי מאי דמסקינן לקמן האי "כל" ריבוי הוא, מדלא כתיב הני פרטי גבי כסף וכלים, וס"ל דכפל ושבועה הכל אחד — ניחא, דליכא אלא חד קרא לתרוייהו. וא"ת: וגניבה בקרקע היכי שייכא? וי"ל: במשיג גבול; א"נ במחובר לקרקע, כי ההיא די' גפנים טעונות, וטוען שנגנבו לו ה', ונמצא שהוא גנבם (שבועות ד' מב:):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:15:1.english: "Land is excluded, etc." - And if you ask: Since they are excluded from an oath, as we say in the chapter [entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 57b), let it follow automatically that there is no double payment for them in [the case of] one who claims a thief stole [the deposit], for he does not pay [double] except with an oath, as we say later in our sugya? And one cannot say that [the exclusion] was needed for one who jumps and swears [on his own], for in HaGozel Kama (later, Bava Kamma 106a) it is proven that he does not pay [double] unless the court administers the oath to him. And one can answer that it was needed for a case where he swears via devolution of an oath [gilgul shevuah], as we learned in the Mishnah (Kiddushin 26a): "Properties that have security [i.e., real estate] attach to properties [that do not have security,] etc., to take an oath upon them." However, according to what we conclude later—[that] this [word] "all" is an inclusion, since these details are not written with regard to "silver or vessels," and we hold that double payment and an oath are all one—it is satisfactory, for there is only one verse for both of them. And if you ask: How does theft apply to land? One can answer: In [the case of] one who encroaches on a boundary [masig gevul]; or alternatively, in [the case of] something attached to the ground, like that [case] of ten laden vines, where he claims that five were stolen from him, and it turns out that he himself stole them (Shevuot 42b).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:15:2.hebrew: יצאו שטרות - ואם תאמר: למה לי קרא למעט מכפל? והא אפי' אבדו בידים לא משלם קרן למאן דלא דאין דינא דגרמי, ואפי' מאן דדאין לא הוו אלא מדרבנן, כדפרישית בסוף [הפרה] (ד' נד. ד"ה חמור). וי"ל: כיון דאי איתיה לשטר בעין חייב להחזיר (משלם), סלקא דעתך דכשמחזיר [משלם] (מחזיר) הכפל עמו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:15:2.english: "Documents are excluded" - And if you should ask: Why do I need a verse to exclude [documents] from double payment? For even if one destroyed it directly, he does not pay the principal according to the one who does not adjudicate liability for causative damage [dina degarmi], and even [according to] the one who does adjudicate [it], they are only [liable] by rabbinic law, as I explained at the end of [the chapter] HaParah (54a, s.v. Chamor). And one can answer: Since if the document is extant, he is obligated to return [it] (variant: pays), you might have thought that when he returns [it], he pays (variant: returns) the double payment along with it:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:15:3.hebrew: רעהו אמר רחמנא - ולא הקדש. תימה לר"י: ומאי איצטריך "רעהו" למעוטי הקדש מכפל בטוען טענת גנב? הא ליכא שבועה בהקדש! ולמסקנא דנפיק כפל ושבועה מחד קרא, א"ש. וא"ת: דלקמן נפקא לן בפרקין (ד' עו.) למעט הקדש מ"וגונב מבית האיש" — ולא מבית הקדש! וי"ל: דהתם נמי לא מ"איש" קדריש, דגבי הקדש נמי שייך לשון "איש" — ולא משום דכתיב (שמות טו) "ה' איש מלחמה", אלא משום דבכל דבר שהוא לשון זכר שייך לשון "איש", ו"אשה" על לשון נקבה, כגון "אשה אל אחותה" בקרסים (שם כו). אלא התם ה"פ: "מבית איש" — דשייך ביה "רעהו", כדכתיב, ולא מבית הקדש; ואגב דגבי גנב איצטריך למנקט האי לישנא למידרש "ולא מבית הגנב", נקט ליה נמי לענין הקדש:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:15:3.english: The Merciful One said "his neighbor" - and not consecrated property. This is surprising to the Ri: why is "his neighbor" needed to exclude consecrated property from double payment in [the case of] one who makes a claim of theft? Surely there is no oath regarding consecrated property! And according to the conclusion, that double payment and the oath are derived from one verse, it works out well. And if you will ask: later in our chapter (76a) we derive [the rule] to exclude consecrated property from "and it is stolen from the house of the man" — [meaning] and not from the house of consecrated property! One can answer: there too, it does not expound [this] from "man," for regarding consecrated property too the term "man" is applicable — and not because it is written (Exodus 15) "The Lord is a man of war," rather because for anything that is grammatically masculine the term "man" is applicable, and "woman" for the feminine, such as "a woman to her sister" regarding the clasps (ibid. 26). Rather, there this is its explanation: "from the house of a man" — to whom "his neighbor" applies, as it is written, and not from the house of consecrated property; and incidentally, since regarding a thief it was necessary to use this wording to expound "and not from the house of the thief," it used it also regarding consecrated property.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:5:1.hebrew: פסולה כסוכה וכמבוי - תימה דהוה ליה למימר ימעט, כדאמרי' בריש מסכת סוכה (דף ב.): "מבוי דרבנן תני תקנתא". וי"ל: משום דבעי למימר כסוכה נקט לשון פסולה; אי נמי, לפי שהיה צריך להאריך בלשון ולומר יכבה וימעט ויחזור וידליק, דלמעט כמו שהיא מודלקת לא סגי, כדאמרינן בפ' במה מדליקין (שבת דף כב:): "הדליקה בפנים והוציאה בחוץ לא עשה ולא כלום", והכא נמי לא שנא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:5:1.english: [It is] unfit, like a sukkah and like an alleyway - It is puzzling, for he should have said "he should lower [it]," as we say at the beginning of Tractate Sukkah (2a): "[Regarding] an alleyway, which is rabbinic, [the Tanna] teaches a remedy." And one can answer: Because he wanted to say "like a sukkah," he used the expression "unfit"; alternatively, because he would have had to lengthen his wording and say "he should extinguish [it], lower [it], and relight [it]," since lowering [it] while it is [already] lit does not suffice, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 22b): "If one lit it inside and took it outside, he has done nothing," and here too there is no difference.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:7:1.hebrew: מרובה - מי קתני: "אין בין" כו'. משמע הכא, היכא דתני "אין בין", לא שייך למימר "תנא ושייר". והקשה הר"י מאורלינ"ש מהא דתנן בפ"ק דמגילה (ד' ח. ושם ד"ה אין): "אין בין נדרים לנדבות אלא שהנדרים חייב באחריותן, ונדבות אינו חייב באחריותן"; ואכתי, הא איכא שהנדבה באה מן המעשר, ונדר — שהוא דבר שבחובה — אין באה אלא מן החולין, כדתנן בהתודה (מנחות ד' פא.)! וי"ל, דהתם לא בא לשנות כל ענין שנדר ונדבה חלוקים זה מזה, אלא בא לומר שאין חיוב הבאה בזה יותר מבזה, אלא אחריות; אבל לענין בל תאחר, זה וזה שוין. וכן "אין בין שבת ליום הכפורים" — לא איירי לכל דברים שביניהם, כגון איסור אכילה. וכן "אין בין י"ט לשבת אלא אוכל נפש בלבד" — לא איירי בחומר שבשניהם, כגון לאו ומיתה, אלא בדבר האסור או מותר לעשות בהן. ועוד י"ל, דהך משנה דמגילה שנויה במסכת קנים (פ"א מ"א) גבי עולת העוף; ועולה, בין נדר בין נדבה, אין באה מן המעשר, כיון דאין בה אכילת אדם, כדדריש בסיפרי בפ' עשר תעשר: ת"ל "ואכלת ושמחת" — שמחה שיש בה אכילה, יצאו עולות שאין עמהן אכילה. ואין להאריך כאן יותר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 62b:7:1.english: Greater [is the measure...] - [The Gemara asks:] "Does it teach, 'There is no [difference] between...' etc.?" It is implied here [that] wherever [the Mishnah] teaches "There is no [difference] between...," it is not applicable to say "[the Tanna] taught [some cases] and omitted [others]." And Rabbi Yitzchak of Orléans raised a difficulty from that which we learned in the first chapter of Megillah (8a, and there, s.v. Ein): "There is no [difference] between vows (nedarim) and freewill offerings (nedavot) except that [with] vows one is liable for their replacement [if lost], whereas [with] freewill offerings one is not liable for their replacement." Yet still, is there not [another difference], that a freewill offering may come from [second] tithe [funds], whereas a vow — which is an obligatory matter — may come only from non-sacred [funds], as we learned in [the chapter entitled] HaTodah (Menachot 81a)? And one can answer that there [in Megillah], it did not come to teach every matter in which a vow and a freewill offering differ from one another; rather, it came to say that there is no [difference in] obligation of bringing in one more than the other, except [regarding] liability [for replacement] — but regarding [the prohibition of] "do not delay," both this and that are equal. And similarly, [in the Mishnah] "There is no [difference] between Shabbat and Yom Kippur [except...]," it does not speak of all things that are between them, such as the prohibition of eating. And similarly, [in the Mishnah] "There is no [difference] between a Festival and Shabbat except [the preparation of] food for human consumption alone," it does not speak of the severity of both [days], such as [violating] a negative commandment versus the death penalty, but rather of what is forbidden or permitted to do on them. And furthermore, one can answer that this Mishnah in Megillah is taught in Tractate Kinnim (1:1) regarding a bird burnt-offering; and a burnt-offering, whether a vow or a freewill offering, does not come from [second] tithe [funds], since it does not involve human consumption, as [the Sifrei] expounds in Sifrei on the portion of Asser te'asser: The verse states, "And you shall eat... and you shall rejoice" — a rejoicing that involves eating, excluding burnt-offerings which do not involve eating. And there is no [need] to elaborate further here.
